newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goldfields sees delay on Sth Talbot.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goldfields sees delay on Sth Talbot.

text.p: SYDNEY, Oct 29 Reuter - Goldfields Ltd said on Tuesday mining was likely to be delayed at South Talbot, five kms (three miles) from its Paddington mine in Western Australia, by negotiations on Native Title claims.
Chairman Tony Cotton told the annual general meeting the area at South Talbot showed a resource of more than four million tonnes at over two grams of gold a tonne.
Goldfields was upgrading this to reserve status and had been planning to begin mining in February, 1997 he said.
However, Cotton said the area had been covered by four native title claims and Goldfields had four months to conduct negotiations.
He said it was "our guess at the moment" that the company would not be able to reach agreement in the four months.
The parties would then have to go to the Native Title Tribunal to resolve the claims, which would take a minimum of six months.
However, Cotton said the company had been able to work with aboriginal groups successfully in other areas, and expected the claims would be resolved.
Asked later about mine life at Paddington, managing director Peter Cassidy said he believed a portion of the 50,000 tonnes of resource would be converted to reserves.
"That will lift the life (of the mine) from the present five years to, I believe, in excess of 10 years," he said.
